g.title: ap-ceiling-01 [switch] namespace: hosts Ceiling access point above the machine room, powered over its uplink: 'powered_by: poe' says the run carrying its traffic is its only power path, so it declares no 'power.inputs' at all. The far end of that run is sw-access-01:GigabitEthernet1/0/1, reached across pp-r2-a — a run through a panel is electrically one run for power exactly as it is for frames. labels: env=prod, role=wireless, site=hq vlans: 10 interfaces (4): br0 bridge Vlan10 vlan 10.10.0.4/24 vlan 10 (access) eth0 ethernet vlan 10 (access) 70:69:5a:0c:00:01 wlan0 wifi 70:69:5a:0c:00:10 links (2): eth0 — network/sw-access-01:GigabitEthernet1/0/1 (cable, copper, 1Gbps) vlan 10 wlan0 — hosts/laptop-lobby:wlan0 (cable, wireless, 1200Mbps) vlan 10

g.title: sw-access-01 [switch] namespace: network PoE access switch in rack r2. Its uplink leaves the rack through the panel above it, exactly as the server links do; its two PoE ports feed a ceiling access point and a lobby camera, neither of which has a power cord. The switch itself is dual-corded: 'psu1' to the A-side strip, 'psu2' to the B-side one. Both strips are in this rack, and they are on different input feeds, which is what makes 'redundant: true' true (NV-E015). labels: env=prod, role=access, site=hq vlans: 10 interfaces (5): br0 bridge Vlan10 vlan 10.10.0.3/24 vlan 10 (access) GigabitEthernet1/0/1 ethernet vlan 10 (access) 00:1b:0d:0b:00:01 GigabitEthernet1/0/2 ethernet vlan 10 (access) 00:1b:0d:0b:00:02 GigabitEthernet1/0/24 ethernet vlan 10 (access) 00:1b:0d:0b:00:18 links (3): GigabitEthernet1/0/24 — network/sw-core-01:GigabitEthernet1/0/2 (cable, copper, 1Gbps) vlan 10 GigabitEthernet1/0/1 — hosts/ap-ceiling-01:eth0 (cable, copper, 1Gbps) vlan 10 GigabitEthernet1/0/2 — hosts/cam-lobby-01:eth0 (cable, copper, 1Gbps) vlan 10
